description: Statement and Conclusion is a crucial part of Logical Reasoning. It involves accepting the given statement as one hundred percent true and deriving the correct conclusion based purely on logical analysis.

sections.title: Basic Concepts
sections.description: It is essential to understand the exact meanings of statements and conclusions and the logical relationship between them.

key_concepts.explanation: The given information or fact, which must always be assumed to be absolutely true, even if it contradicts commonly known facts.
The direct and logical consequence drawn from the statement. It is a fact that can be definitively said to be true based on the statement.
A conclusion that is explicitly stated or can be directly understood from the words used in the statement.
A conclusion that is not directly written but is based on the hidden meaning or logical deduction of the statement.

sections.title: Rules for Drawing Conclusions
sections.description: To identify a true and valid conclusion, certain fundamental rules must be strictly followed.

results: The conclusion must always lie strictly within the boundary of the statement.
Do not use outside knowledge or personal opinions to judge the conclusion.
A valid conclusion must always be definite.
If a conclusion is merely a possibility or a guess, it is considered invalid (unless the statement itself implies a possibility).
Conclusions containing extreme words like 'Only', 'Always', 'All', 'Never', or 'Definitely' are usually incorrect (unless such extremity is mentioned in the statement).

sections.title: Steps to Solve Questions
sections.description: A systematic approach to solving Statement and Conclusion questions to ensure maximum accuracy in exams.

steps.title: Deep Analysis of the Statement
steps.detail: Read the statement carefully and understand its core message. Focus only on what is strictly written.

steps.title: Separate Evaluation of Conclusion
steps.detail: Read each conclusion individually and check if it aligns directly with the information provided in the statement.

steps.title: Check Logical Connection
steps.detail: Verify if the conclusion is logically derived from the statement. If two statements are given, see if a combined conclusion can be drawn from both.

steps.title: Selection of Options
steps.detail: Choose the correct option based on your analysis, such as 'Only I Follows', 'Both Follow', or 'Neither Follows'.

sections.title: Role of Important Keywords
sections.description: Understanding the logical impact of specific words frequently used in statements and conclusions.

key_concepts.explanation: As a general rule, if a statement is positive, a definitive negative conclusion cannot usually be drawn from it.
If the statement talks about 'Some' parts of a category, a conclusion claiming 'All' for that entire category will be false.
If the statement is a piece of advice, a rule, or a government notice, the logical conclusion is that people will generally follow it or that there is a valid reason behind it.

sections.title: Common Mistakes and Prevention
sections.description: Common errors made by students and techniques to avoid them during examinations.

results: An assumption is what is thought before saying the statement, while a conclusion is the final result deduced after the statement. Do not treat a conclusion as an assumption.
If the statement says 'All tables are chairs', assume it to be completely true. Do not try to invalidate it by applying your real-world General Knowledge.
